newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss Q1 GDP down 0.7 pct yr/yr, Q2 -0.5 - UBS poll.
newsitem.headline: Swiss Q1 GDP down 0.7 pct yr/yr, Q2 -0.5 - UBS poll.

text.p: A quarterly UBS survey of 300 industrial companies indicated Swiss gross domestic product would contract by 0.7 percent in the first quarter and by 0.5 percent in the second quarter from the year-earlier periods.

"The Swiss economy shows itself to be grey on grey again in the first quarter of the current year. But there are increasing signs that suggest the business cycle's lethargic condition is ending," the bank said in a comment on its findings.

In contrast to previous quarters, only one of the three major factors in the indicator -- orders on hand -- was below the year-earlier level for the first quarter, it said, adding output and order inflow were seen stabilising.
"Although participants in the survey expressed somewhat more optimism for the second quarter, the indicator still signals subdued economic activity," it said.

GDP dropped a provisional 0.6 percent year-on-year in the fourth quarter of 1996, close to the 0.5 percent dip forecast by the UBS indicator. But GDP was flat compared with the third quarter, snapping a string of seven consecutive quarterly drops.
GDP contracted 0.7 percent in 1996. The Swiss National Bank and government forecast it will grow 0.5 percent in 1997.

The UBS survey showed sharp differences in industrial sectors in the first quarter of 1997. Production and sales were growing sharply at chemical, pharmaceutical and food companies, and paper and textile companies also reported higher output.

Clothing companies were clearly at the opposite end of the range, and others reporting lower output and turnover included watchmakers, the wood and furniture sector, the metal industry and the printing and graphics sector.
Domestic order inflow dropped in all sectors except food compared with a year earlier, but foreign orders grew nearly across the board, the poll found.
For the second quarter, the most optimistic responses came from the textile, food, and chemical/pharmaceutical sectors, while clothing, printing and watch companies were the most pessismistic.
The 75 construction companies surveyed showed orders on hand, sales, profits, construction volume, personnel and prices were "clearly in negative territory" in the first quarter.
Retailers were stagnant in the first quarter, but expected business to pick up in the course of the year. Turnover was expected to stabilise in the second quarter from a year earlier.
The 1996/97 winter season appears to have gone well for the tourism industry, and most resorts were optimistic for the summer season as well, it said.
